_meta.note: Editorial prose for the generated LLM <slug>-pricing.html provider pages (equivalent of automation/data/pricing-editorial.json). NEVER write prices here — every price/number on the page is generated from llm/data/models.json via the engine. This file holds prose only: a neutral intro, a gotcha warning, 'when worth it' rows, and price-free FAQ. Any answer that needs a live price is generated by the module, not stored here.
_meta.tone: Faceless, neutral, legally fair. No 'best', no superlatives, no disparaging competitors. State trade-offs as facts. Verbs like 'fits', 'consider', 'check' rather than 'use X / avoid Y' marketing language.

conventions.intro: 1-2 sentences: when this provider is a reasonable choice (neutral, fact-based, NO price). Would feed {{INTRO}} in _provider-template.html page-head.
conventions.warn: optional gotcha box — HTML allowed, NO hardcoded price (engine appends real figures where useful). One thing a buyer could trip over.
conventions.whenWorthIt: list of {case, verdict, tier} rows; tier = good|warn|bad → coloured cell. 2-3 per provider.
conventions.faq: list of {q, a} — a is HTML, NO prices (price-bearing FAQ rows are appended by the module). 2-3 per provider.

_meta.source_of_facts: llm/data/models.json (verified 2026-06-20). Do not restate exact prices here; reference behaviour only.

openai.intro: OpenAI offers a broad GPT-5 lineup spanning frontier, mid and budget tiers, all with prompt caching and batch discounts, plus a high-end Pro variant for the most demanding reasoning tasks.
openai.warn: The top-end GPT-5.5 Pro tier is listed without a cached-input rate, so prompt caching can't be assumed to lower its cost — price it on full input. Both flagship tiers also carry a separate long-context rate for very large prompts; check which rate applies to your prompt size before estimating.

whenWorthIt.case: You want one vendor covering frontier down to budget models with a consistent API
Workload is asynchronous and tolerant of delay
whenWorthIt.verdict: Batch tier lowers the per-token cost

whenWorthIt.case: Hard requirement for the lowest possible token price
whenWorthIt.verdict: Compare against budget-tier and open-weight providers in the table

faq.q: Does OpenAI support prompt caching and batch processing?
faq.a: Most GPT-5 tiers offer both a discounted cached-input rate and a batch (async) discount. The exception in our data is the top Pro tier, which is listed without a cached rate — see the per-model table above for which models include caching.

faq.q: Why do some OpenAI models show a separate long-context price?
faq.a: The flagship tiers apply a higher rate to very large prompts (above a token threshold) than to short prompts. The table shows the standard short-context rate; if your prompts are large, model the long-context rate noted on the page instead.

anthropic.intro: Anthropic's Claude lineup runs from a frontier Fable/Opus tier down to a budget Haiku tier, with prompt caching and batch discounts available across the range and a large context window on most models.
anthropic.warn: Caching and batch behaviour is consistent across the lineup, but the budget tier ships with a smaller context window than the frontier and mid tiers — confirm the window on the model you pick matches your longest prompt.

whenWorthIt.case: Long documents or large context within a single request
whenWorthIt.verdict: Most Claude tiers carry a large context window

whenWorthIt.case: Repeated system prompts or shared context across calls
whenWorthIt.verdict: Prompt caching applies across the lineup

whenWorthIt.case: You need the cheapest tier with maximum context
whenWorthIt.verdict: Check the budget tier's smaller window first

faq.q: Is prompt caching available on every Claude tier?
faq.a: Caching and a batch (async) discount are available across the lineup in our data. The discounted cached-input rate per tier is shown in the per-model table above.

faq.q: Do all Claude models have the same context window?
faq.a: No — the frontier and mid tiers carry the larger context window, while the budget tier is smaller. The exact window per model is listed in the context-window note on this page.

google.intro: Google's Gemini lineup pairs a frontier Pro tier with several Flash tiers, all offering a large context window, prompt caching and batch discounts, which suits workloads that mix high-volume and reasoning-heavy calls.
google.warn: The frontier Gemini 3.1 Pro tier applies a higher rate to prompts above roughly 200k tokens than to shorter prompts. The table shows the standard short-context rate — if your prompts routinely exceed that threshold, model the long-context rate noted on the page instead, or the estimate will run low.

whenWorthIt.case: High-volume calls where a budget Flash tier is enough
You need a large context window across most tiers
Prompts regularly exceed the long-context threshold on the Pro tier
whenWorthIt.verdict: Budget for the higher long-context rate

faq.q: When does Gemini's long-context surcharge apply?
faq.a: On the frontier Pro tier, prompts above a token threshold are billed at a higher rate than shorter prompts. The table reflects the standard short-context rate; the long-context note on this page shows the higher tier.

faq.q: Do Gemini models support caching and batch processing?
faq.a: Across the lineup in our data, the models offer a discounted cached-input rate and a batch (async) discount. Per-model figures are in the table above.

deepseek.intro: DeepSeek offers open-weight models at some of the lowest per-token rates in this comparison, with a large context window and a very steep cached-input discount, which suits high-volume or cost-sensitive workloads.
deepseek.warn: DeepSeek V4 Pro's headline rate reflects a standing promotional discount (roughly 75% off). If that promotion ends, the list price would step up several-fold — treat the current rate as promotional rather than permanent when you forecast a long-term budget.

whenWorthIt.verdict: DeepSeek's rates are among the lowest here
The cached-input discount is very steep

whenWorthIt.case: You need a stable multi-year price guarantee
whenWorthIt.verdict: Account for the promotional rate possibly ending

faq.q: Is DeepSeek's low price a permanent rate?
faq.a: The flagship Pro tier's rate reflects a standing promotional discount in our data. It has been in place for some time, but it is a promotion — if it ends, the list price would be materially higher. Budget for that risk on long-running workloads.
Our data does not list a separate batch (async) discount for DeepSeek, so batch is not assumed in the estimate. The steep cached-input rate is the main lever for lowering cost — see the table above.

xai.intro: xAI's Grok models offer a flagship tier with a large context window and a low output-to-input price ratio, plus a flat cached-input rate, which can suit output-heavy workloads.
xai.warn: xAI publishes a Batch API but does not publish the exact discount multiplier, so we hold no batch figure and the estimate does not assume one — your real async cost may be lower than shown. The cached-input rate is also flat across tiers rather than scaling with the standard rate.

whenWorthIt.verdict: Grok's output rate is relatively low versus input

whenWorthIt.case: Large context within a single request
whenWorthIt.verdict: The flagship tier carries a large window

whenWorthIt.case: You need a confirmed batch discount up front
whenWorthIt.verdict: The exact batch multiplier is unpublished

faq.q: Does xAI offer a batch discount?
faq.a: xAI documents a Batch API, but the exact discount is not published in a form we can verify, so we hold no batch figure and the estimate does not apply one. Your async cost may be lower than the on-demand figure shown.
Our data lists a flat cached-input rate across the Grok tiers rather than one that scales with each model's standard rate. The exact figure is in the per-model table above.

mistral.intro: Mistral is the European option in this comparison; its publicly priced flagship, Mistral Large 3, offers caching and a batch discount at a low per-token rate with a sizeable context window.
mistral.warn: The Mistral Large 3 rate reflects a promotional price rather than a settled long-term list price, so treat it as subject to change when forecasting. Mistral's wider lineup (mid, small and specialised models) does not yet have verified public per-token pricing in our data, so only the flagship is shown.

whenWorthIt.case: You want an EU-based vendor for data-residency reasons
whenWorthIt.verdict: Mistral is the European option here

whenWorthIt.case: A single flagship model covers your needs
whenWorthIt.verdict: Mistral Large 3 with caching and batch fits

whenWorthIt.case: You need a budget or specialised tier with a verified public price
whenWorthIt.verdict: Only the flagship is currently verifiable

faq.q: Why does Mistral show only one model?
faq.a: Only the flagship tier has a verified public per-token price in our data. Mistral's wider lineup (mid, small and specialised models) is expected to be added once its public per-token rates and context windows are confirmed.

faq.q: Is the Mistral Large 3 price stable?
faq.a: It reflects a promotional rate rather than a settled long-term list price, so treat it as subject to change for long-running budgets. The current figure and whether caching and batch apply are shown in the table above.
